properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 30 at 12:03PM PDT until November 2 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...A moderate risk for sneaker waves is expected. A building
west-northwest long period swell is expected to combine with
lowering west-northwest swell and a south swell.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These
waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and sweep
them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Avoid climbing on rocks and jetties. Stay away from the ocean and
remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT
Saturday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 8 PM EDT this
evening through Sunday evening. For the High Surf Advisory,
from 2 PM Saturday to 7 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper

properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef
National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake
Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread moderate to at times heavy precipitation is expected
across much of southern, southeast and east central Utah
beginning late Saturday night, and continuing throughout the day
Sunday.

Moist antecedent conditions from recent heavy rains will result
in efficient and excessive runoff, allowing all area washes,
streams and rivers to run fast and high. Flood prone areas will
likely become inundated at times, and backcountry roads will
likely become impassable from this excessive runoff.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

and minimum relative humidity values near 40 percent will lead to
an elevated risk of fire spread across the Lower Hudson Valley
during the late morning and afternoon today.

Use extra caution if handling any potential ignition sources such
as machinery or matches, and ensure to properly extinguish or
dispose of cigarette butts. Any fires that ignite will have the
potential to spread quickly.

This forecast considers meteorological, fuel, and land conditions
and has been developed in coordination with state fire and land
management officials.

For more information about wildfire danger and wildfire
prevention, please visit the New York Department of Environmental
Conservation website at...
